thread_analysis.thread_summary: Alinco Qualcomm-based module registration. The product is Class 1 (high power). Setting RF ICS item 1/1 = Supported triggers an unresolvable Invalid because the Check Rule mandates LMP 31/1 (Power Control), which the QDID does not support. Solution: set RF 1/1 = NO (Class 2 in RF layer) and RF PHY 1/15 = YES (PHY Class 1) — this accurately represents Class 1 capability without triggering the LMP dependency. RF/RF PHY test must be conducted at Class 1 settings.

thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: SIG Check Rule: 'If RF(1/1) Supported then LMP(31/1) Mandatory.' LMP 31/1 = LMP Power Control. If the QDID used does not include LMP 31/1, setting RF 1/1 = Supported creates an unresolvable Invalid. The correct approach for Class 1 modules: RF 1/1 = NO (avoids LMP dependency) + RF PHY 1/15 = YES (PHY Class 1 = expresses Class 1 output at the PHY layer, no LMP dependency). RF/RF PHY test conducted at Class 1 power settings to match the RF PHY 1/15 ICS entry.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: Check QDID for LMP 31/1 support before setting RF 1/1 = Supported. If LMP 31/1 not supported → use RF 1/1 = NO + RF PHY 1/15 = YES. Confirm test settings match RF PHY ICS (Class 1 test for RF PHY 1/15 = YES).
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Setting RF 1/1 = Supported when LMP 31/1 is unavailable blocks the registration with an unresolvable Invalid. Setting RF 1/1 = NO without RF PHY 1/15 = YES produces an inaccurate ICS that understates the product's power class.
thread_analysis.consulting_mistake: Setting RF 1/1 = Supported for Class 1 modules without first checking whether the QDID supports LMP 31/1. The RF vs. RF PHY distinction for power class representation is non-obvious and commonly misunderstood.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: For any Class 1 module: standard ICS pattern is RF 1/1 = NO + RF PHY 1/15 = YES. Confirm this pattern at ICS setup and align the RF test plan to Class 1 (PHY Class 1) settings before testing begins.
